title: Inheritance and Parish
premise: Estate lawyer Isandro Reyes is summoned to a decaying manor in the Fenlow valley to read the will of Edric Vane, only to discover the will names a beneficiary who has been legally dead for eleven years. Twin letters arrive — one confessing to a buried crime, one promising 'more' if she keeps reading — and Isandro realizes the confession was written by someone who shouldn't be alive. As the trial of the Vane estate's true killer approaches, she must locate the vanished witness, Maren Vane, before opposing counsel buries her forever. Isandro finds Maren hiding in plain sight as the parish sexton, learns the price Maren paid to survive, and must choose between handing her to the court or letting justice outside the law stand; in the end, she reads a second will aloud that forces the truth into daylight, and the guilty are undone by their own signatures.
about_author: Beatrix Amberdale is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wills, deeds, and quiet scandals in rural England. She writes mysteries where paperwork is more dangerous than pistols.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro Reyes arrives at Vane Manor to execute the will of Edric Vane and finds it names Maren Vane — declared dead eleven years ago. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Two letters arrive at Isandro's office: one confessing to a crime from eleven years past, unsigned but unmistakably in Maren's hand; the other promising 'more' if she continues. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Parish Register
chapters.summary: Isandro searches the church records and finds Maren's death entry forged by the old vicar, now senile and living above the vestry. He mistakes her for his dead sister. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: first crack in the village's united silence.

chapters.title: What the Family Swears
chapters.summary: At the manor, Edric's brother Aldous and niece Cordelia insist Maren drowned, offering a funeral photograph as proof. The photograph shows an empty coffin. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: polite menace beneath tea and silverware.

chapters.title: A Grave Without a Body
chapters.summary: Isandro opens the Vane plot with the gravedigger's reluctant help: the coffin holds river stones and a woman's boot. Someone paid for silence then, someone pays now. POV: gravedigger Tom Ellery. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing after years underwater.

chapters.title: The Confession Read Twice
chapters.summary: Studying the confession, Isandro notices details only a witness could know — and a second handwriting beneath, corrections made by someone else. Two authors. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the case turns from inheritance to murder.

chapters.title: Counsel for the Dead
chapters.summary: Opposing lawyer Harrow Blake appears, retained by Cordelia, and warns Isandro off with surgical courtesy. He already knows about the letters. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: realizing she is being watched, not warned.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Winter
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Maren Vane flees the manor the night of the crime, half-drowned in the fen, saved by the sexton who gives her his dead wife's name and clothes. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: survival purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Hands
chapters.summary: Back in the present, Isandro observes the current sexton — a woman with a lawyer's calluses on her pen finger, not a spade's. She says nothing, but leaves the church door unlocked. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: recognition without proof.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: The court calendar lands: the trial of the accused handyman, Silas Crane, begins in six weeks. Isandro realizes the letters were timed to force her hand before then. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Silas in the Dock
chapters.summary: Visiting Silas Crane in custody, Isandro finds a broken man who confessed to protect someone he won't name. He asks only that she tell Maren the dog died happy. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice revealed as love.

chapters.title: More
chapters.summary: The second letter's promise arrives: pages of the true account, mailed in installments, each ending mid-sentence. The latest names Aldous. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: complicity deepening — she is now part of the story.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro discovers Cordelia has been quietly selling off estate land, needing the trial concluded fast to clear title. Motive surfaces: not hatred, but debt. POV: Cordelia. Emotional beat: sympathy for a woman drowning respectably.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Last Rites
chapters.summary: The old vicar dies, and among his papers Isandro finds the original forgery fee receipt — signed by Aldous Vane. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by grief for the man who almost told her everything.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Blake offers Isandro a partnership and a share of the estate fees if the witness stays lost. She declines; that night her office is searched. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the price of integrity made literal.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Following the sexton after evensong, Isandro corners Maren in the bell tower. Maren admits everything except forgiveness — for herself. POV: both, alternating. Emotional beat: two women deciding whether truth is worth the cost.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Maren explains why she stayed hidden: testifying would have destroyed Silas's alibi and freed Aldous; her silence kept him safe and herself erased. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Aldous Closes In
chapters.summary: Aldous, tipped off by the office break-in, confronts Maren at the churchyard with a pistol and an offer: leave tonight and live, stay and be buried properly this time. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Isandro invokes an obscure probate clause to read a supplementary testament — the confession itself, executed as a sworn declaration — before the assembled family and Blake. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the law turned against its abusers.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Aldous flees across the fen toward the boat he kept for eleven years; the ground, the fog, and Tom Ellery's shovel decide what the court cannot. POV: Tom. Emotional beat: grim communal verdict, no verdict spoken.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: At trial, Maren Vane takes the stand under her own name; Silas walks free, and Cordelia surrenders the estate rather than face fraud charges. Blake withdraws without apology. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: weary, imperfect vindication.

chapters.title: Inheritance and Parish
chapters.summary: Months later, Maren tends the parish garden under her own name; Isandro files the closed case and keeps the twin letters, unanswered. Some inheritances are debts. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: quiet peace earned, not given.
